preconditions.description: The number of test cases t must be between 1 and 10,000.
For each test case, the number of vertices n must be between 1 and 400,000, and the number of edges m must be between 0 and 400,000.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= a_i <= n and 1 <= b_i <= n for a_i, b_i in edges)
preconditions.description: All edges must connect valid vertices within the range from 1 to n.

postconditions.description: The output must be a sequence of n integers for each test case, separated by spaces.

postconditions.expression: all(result in {-1, 0, 1, 2} for result in results)
postconditions.description: Each result for the vertices must be one of the values -1, 0, 1, or 2.
The number of results must match the number of vertices n for each test case.
The output for each vertex must correctly reflect the number of paths from vertex 1 to that vertex: 0 for no paths, 1 for exactly one path, 2 for more than one finite path, and -1 for infinite paths.
postconditions.expression: all((result == 0 and count_paths(1, v) == 0) or (result == 1 and count_paths(1, v) == 1) or (result == 2 and count_paths(1, v) > 1 and count_paths(1, v) < float('inf')) or (result == -1 and count_paths(1, v) == float('inf')) for v, result in enumerate(results, start=1))

repair_issue.instruction: Add a postcondition to ensure that the output for each vertex correctly reflects the number of paths from vertex 1 to that vertex as specified in the task.
repair_issue.task_evidence: For each vertex $v$ output one of four values: $0$, if there are no paths from $1$ to $v$; $1$, if there is only one path from $1$ to $v$; $2$, if there is more than one path from $1$ to $v$ and the number of paths is finite; $-1$, if the number of paths from $1$ to $v$ is infinite.
